title: Review: Variation and evolution
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.6.2-c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c17 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c19 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.6.2-q02, 4.6.2-q06, 4.6.2-q08, 4.6.2-q11, 4.6.2-q15, 4.6.2-q01, 4.6.2-q05, 4.6.2-q09, 4.6.2-q12, 4.6.2-q14, 4.6.2-q03, 4.6.2-q07. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mutation
items.clue: A change in the DNA of an organism.

items.label: Tissue culture
items.clue: Growing identical new plants from small groups of cells.

items.label: Embryo transplants
items.clue: Cells from a developing animal are split apart and placed in host mothers.

questions.stem: Which of these describes the causes of variation between individuals in a population?

options.text: Inherited genes, the conditions of development, or both
Inherited genes alone, which are passed on by the parents
Mutations that are produced by a change in the environment
Mutations alone, because every one changes the phenotype

questions.explanation: Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited, the conditions in which they have developed, or a combination of genes and the environment.

questions.stem: In a beetle population most beetles are pale and a few are dark. The tree bark the beetles live on becomes darker, so birds find the pale beetles more easily. After many generations most of the beetles are dark. Which statement explains this?

options.text: The beetles developed a dark colour because they needed it
Each pale beetle became darker as the tree bark got darker
The darker bark caused the mutations that made beetles darker
Dark beetles survived to breed and passed on their variant

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment, and those beetles pass the genes on to the next generation.

questions.stem: A farmer chooses the cows that produce the most milk and breeds them together. From their offspring he again breeds those that produce the most milk, and he repeats this for many generations. Which statement about this process is correct?

options.text: It is natural selection, as the best cows survive and breed
It is genetic engineering, as the genome is being modified
It is selective breeding, as the farmer chose the parents
It was complete once the first chosen cows had been bred

questions.explanation: Selective breeding is the process by which humans breed animals for particular genetic characteristics, here the useful characteristic of producing more milk.

questions.stem: Which statement about the uses of genetic engineering is correct?

options.text: Bacterial cells have been engineered to make human insulin
Tissue culture is used to insert genes in bacterial cells
Inherited disorders are now cured using genetic modification
Crops are engineered by breeding the best plants together

questions.explanation: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to produce useful substances such as human insulin to treat diabetes.

questions.stem: In adult cell cloning the nucleus is removed from an unfertilised egg cell, the nucleus from an adult skin cell is inserted, and an electric shock makes the egg cell divide to form an embryo. What are the embryo cells like?

options.text: They have the genetic information of the egg donor
They have genetic information varying from the adult
They have an extra gene added from another organism
They have the same genetic information as the skin cell

questions.explanation: These embryo cells contain the same genetic information as the adult skin cell whose nucleus was inserted into the egg cell.

questions.stem: Two plants grown from cuttings of the same parent plant are given different amounts of light. One grows much taller than the other. What does this difference show?

options.text: The plants inherited different genes for their height
The change in light has caused a mutation in one plant
The environment has influenced the phenotype of the plants
One plant has evolved to be taller in the brighter light

questions.explanation: The genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype, so the different light conditions have produced different heights.

options.text: A change in the characteristics of an animal in its lifetime
A change in the inherited characteristics of a population
A change in appearance that makes a population a new species
The growth of the characteristics that organisms need most

questions.explanation: Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection.

questions.stem: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?

options.text: It removes inherited defects from the breeds produced
It happens in wild populations with no human choice
It can lead to inbreeding in the breeds it produces
It adds a gene from another organism to the offspring

questions.explanation: Selective breeding can lead to 'inbreeding' where some breeds are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.

questions.stem: Which statement about genetically modified (GM) crops is correct?

options.text: GM crops generally produce lower yields than other food crops
GM crops are grown from cells taken from one parent plant
GM crops may affect populations of wild flowers and insects
GM crops are used to cure inherited disorders in patients

questions.explanation: Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel the effects on human health have not been fully explored.

questions.stem: A nursery needs many new plants that are identical to one rare parent plant. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A gene from another plant would give identical copies
Tissue culture of the parent's cells gives identical plants
Cuttings from the parent give plants showing variation
One generation of breeding would give identical offspring

questions.explanation: Tissue culture uses small groups of cells from part of a plant to grow identical new plants, which is important for preserving rare plant species.

questions.stem: All variants arise from mutations. Which statement about mutations and phenotype is correct?

options.text: Most mutations lead to a change in the phenotype
Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype
Mutations happen only when the environment changes
Mutations build up in an organism during its life

questions.explanation: Most variants have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.

questions.stem: Two populations of one species have been separated for a very long time and now look very different. What must be shown before they are classed as two new species?

options.text: That their phenotypes are different enough to tell apart
That each population has developed the features that it needs
That the individuals have changed during their own lifetimes
That they can no longer produce fertile offspring together

questions.explanation: Two new species have formed when the populations are so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
